NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - a Gelugpa (Yellow Hat) Tibetan Buddhist monastery, the Lower Gompa of Bomdila; keep-or-drop decision needed. Founded in 1960 by the 12th reincarnate of Tsona Gontse Rinpoche to support Tibetan refugees and preserve the Gelugpa tradition, it is an important centre for circumambulation and prostration by local devotees; a new prayer hall was later blessed by Gaden Tripa Lobsang Tenzin. Coordinates are approximate (district-level geocode match only).

name: Lower Gompa, Bomdila
town_description: Bomdila is a hill town in West Kameng district and the district headquarters, lying on the road between Tezpur (Assam) and Tawang. Known for its Buddhist monasteries - the Upper and Lower Gompas - panoramic Himalayan views and apple orchards, it is the usual overnight stop for travellers heading onward to Tawang.

travel.road: In Bomdila town, about 1 km from the APSTS bus stop; on the Tezpur-Tawang road
